result.summary: Full S1-S14 pass over REQ-021 (waitlist placement with computed position display: getWaitlistPosition + confirmation-message wiring), branch feature/WF02-REQ-021, commit e908344. Read docs/agents/instructions/core-directives.md and security-invariants.md in full, docs/agents/design/REQ-021.md in full, then `git diff master...feature/WF02-REQ-021` myself (13 files: domain/registration.ts, handlers/registration.ts, i18n additions, both test files, design doc, handoffs). Read REVIEWER's step-02b for context only -- re-derived every claim myself. This is a small, low-risk, read-only diff, but ran the complete S1-S14 checklist rather than skipping items, per the mandate that a change touching apps/bot/** always gets a recorded verdict. AUTHORIZATION CHECK (task step 3) -- PASS. getWaitlistPosition(db, eventId, registrationId) (domain/registration.ts:228-272) takes registrationId as its only row-selecting input; the ONLY call site (handlers/registration.ts:101-103) supplies outcome.registrationId, which is populated exclusively by registerForEvent's own same-request INSERT ... RETURNING for the ACTING user's own new row (registration.ts:178-187, unchanged from REQ-020) -- never taken from callback data, never user-suppliable. A malicious/forged callback_data could only vary eventId (matched from `register:`), and eventId is used solely to scope the ahead-count WHERE clause (registrations.eventId = eventId AND admission='waitlisted' AND ahead-of-target) -- it cannot be used to read a different registration's row, because the target row is always looked up by the caller's own registrationId, not by eventId+arbitrary-id. The function's ahead-count query selects only `{ id: registrations.id }` from the ahead-rows and returns only `aheadRows.length + 1` (registration.ts:256-271) -- the ahead rows' own ids, and by extension their owning users' identities, are read into memory but NEVER returned, logged, or surfaced anywhere; only a plain integer leaves the function. Confirmed by reading the full function body and its one caller: no path from getWaitlistPosition's output to anything but a numeric position line in the calling user's own reply message. No cross-user exposure, no enumeration of other users' existence beyond an aggregate count (which S2/S3's own negative cases do not prohibit -- an aggregate count is explicitly the AC1 requirement itself, PRD FR-6). S1 -- N/A, reason: no new personal data is stored or consent-checked by this diff. getWaitlistPosition performs zero writes; the waitlisted registration row itself (source of any consent gating) is written by registerForEvent, unchanged by this diff, and reaching that write already required the existing consent_pd_at gate (established at REQ-016/verified at REQ-020's own security gate, not re-touched here). S2 -- N/A, reason: registration/waitlist-position display has no role/EventStaff authorization surface -- every registered member may see their own waitlist position for an event they themselves registered for; this is not a privileged action (matches REQ-020's own S2 N/A finding, unchanged surface). S3 (PRIMARY FOCUS for this diff) -- PASS. Constructed the negative case directly: could getWaitlistPosition or its caller ever surface a DIFFERENT member's Profile fields or another registrant's identity? Read the full call chain -- registrationId is always the calling user's own just-inserted row (see authorization check above), the function's SELECT columns are `{ createdAt, admission }` for the target row and `{ id }` for ahead rows (registration.ts:235-238, 257) -- no name/phone/email/employer column is read anywhere in this function's two queries. The reply composed in handlers/registration.ts (composeRegistrationReply, lines 111-156) inserts only `waitlistPosition` (a number) and catalog copy into the message -- no other registrant's row, id, or field ever reaches the reply. Re-ran registration.test.ts's two AC1 tests myself (position 1, then position 2 for a second registrant against the same event) -- confirmed each user's own reply names only their own numeric position, never the other's. S4/S5/S6 -- N/A, no qr_token/InviteCode or check-in code touched by this diff. S7 -- N/A, this diff adds no capacity/admission-decision code; getWaitlistPosition is read-only and runs strictly after registerForEvent's transaction has already committed (handlers/registration.ts:64-65 answerCallbackQuery precedes the position read at line 101-103), confirmed by reading the call order myself -- it cannot participate in or race the capacity decision. S8 (checked as directed, task step 5) -- PASS, unchanged. Confirmed decideRegistrationOutcome and registerForEvent (registration.ts:48-74, 109-216) are byte-for-byte unchanged by this diff (`git diff` shows zero lines touched in either function) -- the single writeAuditLog call at registration.ts:201-208 (one row per admitted/waitlisted write, zero on refusal) is untouched. Re-ran registration.db.test.ts's AC7 audit-log block myself (three assertions: exactly-one-row admitted, exactly-one-row waitlisted, zero-row refusal) -- all three passed against real Postgres, confirming this diff introduced no new write path and did not regress the existing one. S9/S10 -- N/A, no notification/scheduler/broadcast code touched. S11 (task step 4) -- PASS. Confirmed by reading getWaitlistPosition's full signature and query columns: it reads only `registrations.createdAt`, `registrations.admission`, and `registrations.id` -- zero profile/PII columns (no phone/email/employer/tg_username) anywhere in either of its two SELECTs. Grepped domain/registration.ts and handlers/registration.ts for any log/console call: zero matches (same as REQ-020's finding, still true after this diff). The new i18n strings (waitlistedPositionPrefix, waitlistedWhatNext) are static catalog copy with a single interpolated integer, never PII. S12 -- N/A, no export code touched. S13 (migration sign-off, task's named duty) -- N/A, no migration in this diff. Confirmed via `git diff master...feature/WF02-REQ-021 --stat` and a direct search for any migrations directory changes: none present, matching REQ-021.md §7's explicit "no schema change" claim (verified independently by reading db/schema.ts myself: registrations.event_id/admission/created_at/id and registrations_waitlist_order_idx all pre-exist REQ-011). No sign-off required; nothing to gate under S13. S14 -- N/A, no speaker/publication code touched. COMPUTED-NEVER-STORED PROPERTY, security-relevance judgment (task step 6) -- my judgment: this property is CORRECTNESS/QA scope, not a security invariant in the S1-S14 sense, and I record why rather than silently filing it under either. None of S1-S14's own negative cases describe a stale-computed-value failure mode (they describe unauthorized access, missing audit rows, guessable tokens, PII leakage, or improper deletion) -- a wrong/stale waitlist number told to a user does not create unauthorized data access, does not leak another user's PII, and does not corrupt an audit trail. It IS a trust/accuracy property (PRD 13 criterion 8's own framing), and I verified it as thoroughly as a security item would be verified -- read §2.4's construction-based argument, then independently re-ran the real-Postgres AC2 test (registration.db.test.ts's byte-identical updated_at assertion before/after a direct SQL admission flip on a DIFFERENT row) myself and confirmed it passes against live Postgres, not a mock. But I classify it outside this gate's S1-S14 scope rather than inventing a 15th invariant unilaterally -- REVIEWER's step-02b (code quality/correctness gate) is the structurally correct owner of this property, and its PASS already independently re-verified the same byte-identical-updated_at claim. Flagging this classification explicitly rather than silently treating REVIEWER's coverage as redundant with mine. Commands run myself, real output: `npm run lint` (repo root) -> exit 0, 0 errors (2 pre-existing unrelated apps/web LCP warnings only, outside apps/bot). `npm run build` (repo root) -> exit 0, both workspaces (apps/web next build, apps/bot tsc) clean. `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` (repo root, full suite) -> 16 files / 178 passed, 0 failures. `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism --reporter=verbose apps/bot/src/domain/registration.db.test.ts` -> 17/17 passed, individually confirmed all four new REQ-021 tests (AC2's live-flip test, two null-case tests, AC4's 6-past-capacity test) ran against real Postgres (dbAvailable=true, no skips reported). No S1-S14 violation found. All applicable items PASS; N/A items stated with reasons above, none silently skipped.
